_doc: GENERIC / ROUTER cabinet (#9, built 2026-07-16 -- the roster's crown jewel). For ANY pipe whose brand has no cabinet yet, and as the HALLMARK service for every brand: a silver-banded pipe with a UK hallmark dates to an EXACT year (or an honest candidate list) regardless of brand. Charts: LONDON (leopard's head) + BIRMINGHAM (anchor) in brand_research/uk_hallmarks/ -- constructed 2026-07-16 from documented cycle rules (silvermakersmarks.co.uk, 925-1000.com, vintagewatchstraps.com) with TWO ANCHORS VERIFIED against our local pipephil mirror (Birmingham lowercase o=1913, uppercase O=1938, the GBD bulldog example). Dublin stays in peterson.json (its fineness boundaries are Dublin-specific). CASE MATTERS: cycles repeat letters and differ by case/font -- the engine matches case-sensitively first and returns honest candidates otherwise; era hints from other channels narrow them. Pre-1975 hallmark years span TWO calendar years (London changed letters in May, Birmingham in July) -> a result year may truly be year-or-year+1 (Green's Comoy examples read '1913/14' for exactly this reason). | 2026-07-18 (Farid: 'general cabinet for the pipes without cabinet'): WIRED as the universal no-brand fallback in Chronos-Pipe cabinet_dating.py (before, it only matched notes saying 'unknown/unbranded' - the 12 NO_BRAND drafts in CABINET_REPORT_DRAFTS_20260718 never reached it). Added windows: Czechoslovakia, USSR, EIRE, Republic-of-Ireland, FOREIGN 1891-1921, 9mm-filter 1934 floor. Farid's law: UNDATED -> the listing says NOTHING about age.

history_anchors._doc: This cabinet holds NO brand history -- it encodes cross-brand physical/legal facts: UK assay date letters (exact years), US import-marking law (origin wording floors), and (future) UK Registered-Design number tables. It is the fallback router: identify_full sends any no-cabinet brand here, and any brand cabinet's confirm-flow can consult it for hallmarks.

brand_marks.physical: UK hallmark cluster = lion passant (sterling) + town mark (leopard's head = London, anchor = Birmingham, Hibernia+harp = Dublin) + date letter (+ duty head pre-1890). Read ALL marks; the date letter's CASE and the town mark are what disambiguate.

assay_hallmark.caveat: bands were bought in batches -> hallmark may predate the pipe by up to ~1-3 years (Green); aftermarket/repair bands exist (Barling guide) -> a hallmark dates the BAND with certainty, the PIPE with high probability. Pre-1975 letters span two calendar years (May/July changeover).

table.note: GERMAN GOODS: 'Germany US-Zone' = occupation era 1945-1949 (verified 2026-07-16: porcelainmarksandmore + antique-trade consensus)
THE German bracket: West-Germany wording = 1949-1990 (preferred from ~1952/55, standard after a 1973 court ruling; reunification 1990 ends it). Opens ANY German pipe -- Vauen etc.
East German mark, mostly post-1973 standard

US McKinley Tariff (1891) forced origin marks on US-bound goods; the common collector rule 'MADE IN = post-1921' is UNRELIABLE (counterexample on file: 1910 Comoy's Cecil 'Made in England', Green) -> 1891 FLOOR only, low confidence
bare 'Made in Germany' is AMBIGUOUS: pre-1949, a non-participating 1949-90 maker, or post-1990 -> floor only; the West-Germany wording above is the sharp one
bare country word = same 1891 floor; wording style is brand-specific -> the BRAND cabinet owns tighter brackets
EIRE marking: 1937 constitution to 1949 Republic; some use ran later - medium

match: made in the republic of ireland

table.note: 'FOREIGN' alone = McKinley-era US import marking window ~1891-1921; intersects with the existing 1891+ floor row

9mm filter system invented 1934 (Vauen Dr. Perl junior, world first - see vauen.json) - hard floor for ANY maker. Lives in com_stamp because the hub feeds free text only to text channels (cabinet_dating.py)

table.label: amber stem = pre-1930 fashion (GBD history: amber/horn dominant before vulcanite spread from late 1870s; approx, verify per brand)
DRGM (Deutsches Reichs-Gebrauchsmuster) = German utility-model mark, 1891-1945 Reich era (validity ran to ~1952 in the FRG) -- standard antiques rule, verify on first live use
DRP (Deutsches Reichs-Patent) = pre-1945 German patent mark
German crescent+crown silver mark (Halbmond und Krone) = 1888+ by law; 800/835/925 fineness typical
